title: Harry Potter Franchise Overview
body:
The Harry Potter franchise began as a series of children's fantasy novels by British author J. K. Rowling, published from 1997, and grew into films, stage plays, games and theme-park attractions. Its public record is unusually well documented: publication dates, film release years, credited authors and studios are matters of public record.

This public edition records only those verifiable facts — titles, creators, dates and formats — in original wording. It contains no copied passages, no lyrics and no script excerpts from the franchise, and it makes no claim about unpublished or private material.

The companion Signature edition is separate fiction. It is labeled throughout as unofficial and unaffiliated, and its stories use original characters and settings inspired by the franchise's themes rather than reproducing its text or claiming official status.

How to use this record: start with the overview, then read the work-by-work records in publication order. Every date and credit below is a public fact; no copyrighted text is reproduced anywhere in this database.

title: Harry Potter Reading and Viewing Order Guide
body:
Recommended public order for the works in this database is publication and release order, beginning with Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997) and ending with Hogwarts Legacy (2023). That order follows how the franchise actually reached the public, and it avoids assuming any later reordering.

The full order is: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997); Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (1998); Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (1999); Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2000); Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (2003); Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (2005); Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (2007); Harry Potter and the Cursed Child (2016); Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them (2016); Hogwarts Legacy (2023). Each title in that list has its own record in this database with its credited creators and format.

This guide contains facts only. It does not reproduce story text, and it does not claim that any Signature continuation belongs in the official order.
